history.summary: NOTE: CSV town 'Koderma' is WRONG - there is no verifiable distinct Bhadrakali temple in Koderma; the famous Bhadrakali Temple is at Itkhori in Chatra district (town corrected to Itkhori). This is a Siddha Peetha on the banks of the Mahane (Mahanad) river, a rare confluence of Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism: a Brahmi-script inscription at the idol's base attributes the black-stone Bhadrakali idol to Pala king Mahendra Pal II (9th-10th century). The complex holds a large Buddhist stupa (Manauti stupa) worshipped as Kotheshwar Nath, footprints of Jain Tirthankara Sheetalnath (found 1983) linked also to Mallinath and Parshvanath, and a Sahasra Shivling engraved with 1,008 miniature shivlings. The 5-foot black-stone idol stands on a raised platform; only priests perform puja. Archaeological excavations have recovered black-stone idols from the Shak-Gupta-Vardhan periods (~1500-1800 years ago). Name linked by legend to Buddha's relatives searching for him ('Itkhoi - lost him here').

name: Bhadrakali Temple, Koderma
town_description: Itkhori is a block headquarters town in Chatra district, Jharkhand, about 38 km northeast of Chatra on the Chatra-Chouparan route. It sits on the banks of the Mahane river amid hills and forests and is a major pilgrimage centre for Hindus, Buddhists and Jains. The town is known for the Bhadrakali temple complex and the Itkhori Mahotsav cultural festival.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaktism), with Buddhist and Jain layers

travel.road: ~35 km east of Chatra town via Chatra-Chouparan road; 0.5 km from Bhaduli village
